newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's Herzog praises Italy's EMU efforts.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Herzog praises Italy's EMU efforts.

text.p: German President Roman Herzog praised Italy on Tuesday for its efforts to implement stability policies aimed at preparing its economy for European monetary union (EMU).

"We Germans follow with great respect how resolutely and sucessfully Italy has devoted itself to stability oriented policies in the last few years," Herzog said in a speech released before he was due to deliver it at a dinner in honour of visiting Italian President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro.
"We are pleased about every member country that fulfils the stability criteria and takes part in the currency union from the outset. That is certainly true for Italy," he said.
Germany, whose participation at the start of EMU was once seen as a certainty, is having difficulty meeting the targets and convincing a sceptical public they will benefit from EMU.
Italy once seemed a longshot, but has made great progress toward meeting the goals and has strong public support.
Still, many Germans are averse to Italy's inclusion in the opening round of EMU, fearing it will make the euro more inflation-prone than the mark.
Germany and France last week denied reports that they were hatching a plot to exclude Italy, and with it Spain, from joining the starting EMU lineup.
European leaders will decide next spring on the starting EMU lineup, based on how well countries meet the Maastricht criteria this year.
Scalfaro is due to hold talks with German Chancellor Helmut Kohl on Wednesday at 1000 GMT on the third day of his visit.
